title: Daily prayer
hookLine: a set time and place for prayer
tomorrow: what's Sunday for, if it's not just the day before Monday?

cards: The alarm goes off, and before your feet touch the floor you've read three messages and one piece of bad news. Morning gets claimed fast. So does night.
Ask people who pray and you'll hear two camps. Some say pick a time and a place and never move it. Others say that's too rigid: real prayer happens anywhere, in the car, at the sink.
Both camps can quote the Bible.

teach.h: CAMP ONE: SAME TIME, SAME PLACE.
teach.b: Camp one: same time, same place. A psalm says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Seven times a day I have given praise to thee." Daniel kneels by his window toward Jerusalem three times a day, even when it's against the king's law.
Jesus says, "enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret." The best case: a set time doesn't depend on mood. On flat days, the habit carries you.

Paul writes three words: "Pray without ceasing." Brother Lawrence, a Carmelite brother who worked in a monastery kitchen, said the noise and clatter of his kitchen didn't keep him from God any more than kneeling did.
The best case: if prayer happens only at seven, God becomes an appointment.
The Church's own practice holds both. The Liturgy of the Hours sets prayer at fixed points from morning to night, so the whole day between them can become prayer.

The fixed times are the fence posts; the rest is the field. The Angelus does both at once: a short prayer traditionally said morning, noon and evening, a fixed time that interrupts whatever you're doing.

how: Catholics pray at set times, such as morning and evening prayer, grace at meals, the Angelus, or the Liturgy of the Hours, and also pray short prayers through the day.

o: prayer said only when you feel close to God
prayer at a set time and place each day
prayers that only priests and nuns must say

p: God in the clatter of the kitchen

s: praying at a set time makes prayer less real
the psalms and Daniel keep set times; the habit carries you on flat days.
Paul tells Christians to pray without ceasing
three words in his first letter to the Thessalonians.

games.q: your roommate says scheduled prayer is fake and she only prays when she feels it. how would the other camp put its best case?
o: a set time carries you on the days you don't feel it.
feelings don't matter to God, so hers don't count.
scheduled prayer is holier, so she's doing it wrong.
games.why: camp one's best case: the habit doesn't depend on mood. and her camp has Paul: pray without ceasing. the Church keeps both.

practice: Choose your time and your place, out loud or on paper: this chair, this hour. Then sit there now, in that spot if you can, and spend the two minutes simply arriving. Nothing to say yet; just learn where it is.

wordCard.voice: Daily prayer. A set time and a set place, so prayer doesn't depend on mood, and the rest of the day can fill in.

orig.note: Greek: without ceasing. Paul's word in 1 Thessalonians 5:17.

carryVoice: Your line: same time, same place. Fence posts first; the field fills in. Talk tomorrow.
